---
title: "The Education Equation"
subtitle: "Does higher education lead to higher income?"
title-block-banner: true
---

```{r}
#| include: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(readr)

states <- read_csv("data/state_acs_2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
florida_counties <- read_csv(
  "data/florida_county_acs_2024.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
county_shapes <- sf::st_read("data/florida_counties.geojson", quiet = TRUE) |>
  sf::st_transform(4326) |>
  select(GEOID)
county_geojson <- jsonlite::fromJSON(
  geojsonsf::sf_geojson(county_shapes),
  simplifyVector = FALSE
)

correlation <- cor(
  states$bachelors_plus_pct,
  states$median_household_income
)
income_model <- lm(
  median_household_income ~ bachelors_plus_pct,
  data = states
)
state_residuals <- states |>
  mutate(income_residual = residuals(income_model))
above_trend <- state_residuals |>
  slice_max(income_residual, n = 1)
below_trend <- state_residuals |>
  slice_min(income_residual, n = 1)
top_education <- states |>
  slice_max(bachelors_plus_pct, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  arrange(bachelors_plus_pct)
top_income <- states |>
  slice_max(median_household_income, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  arrange(median_household_income)
sarasota <- florida_counties |>
  filter(NAME == "Sarasota") |>
  mutate(highlight_value = 1)
```

## The national picture

::: {.chart-card .map-card}
### College graduates across the states

Share of adults age 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher. Hover over a state to compare educational attainment and median household income.

```{r}
#| label: fig-state-map
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

plot_ly(
  data = states,
  type = "choropleth",
  locations = ~abbreviation,
  locationmode = "USA-states",
  z = ~bachelors_plus_pct,
  text = ~paste0(
    "<b>", state, "</b>",
    "<br>Adults with bachelor's degree or higher: ",
    sprintf("%.1f%%", bachelors_plus_pct),
    "<br>Median household income: $",
    scales::comma(median_household_income)
  ),
  hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
  colorscale = list(
    c(0, "#10243A"),
    c(0.52, "#82919A"),
    c(1, "#C8A66A")
  ),
  zmin = 20,
  zmax = 50,
  colorbar = list(title = "Bachelor's or higher (%)"),
  marker = list(line = list(color = "#FAF7F0", width = 0.8))
) |>
  layout(
    geo = list(
      scope = "usa",
      projection = list(type = "albers usa"),
      showlakes = TRUE,
      lakecolor = "#FAF7F0",
      bgcolor = "#FAF7F0"
    ),
    margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, t = 10, b = 0),
    paper_bgcolor = "#FAF7F0",
    font = list(family = "DM Sans", color = "#10243A")
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```
:::

::: {.chart-grid}
::: {.chart-card}
### Education & income

Each point is one state; the dashed line is a descriptive linear trend.

```{r}
#| label: fig-state-relationship
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

trend <- states |>
  arrange(bachelors_plus_pct) |>
  mutate(
    fitted_income = predict(
      income_model,
      newdata = data.frame(bachelors_plus_pct = bachelors_plus_pct)
    )
  )

plot_ly(
  data = states,
  x = ~bachelors_plus_pct,
  y = ~median_household_income,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  text = ~paste0(
    "<b>", state, " (", abbreviation, ")</b>",
    "<br>Adults with bachelor's degree or higher: ",
    sprintf("%.1f%%", bachelors_plus_pct),
    "<br>Median household income: $",
    scales::comma(median_household_income)
  ),
  hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
  marker = list(
    color = "#C8A66A",
    size = 10,
    line = list(color = "#10243A", width = 1)
  )
) |>
  add_trace(
    data = trend,
    x = ~bachelors_plus_pct,
    y = ~fitted_income,
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines",
    name = "Linear trend",
    inherit = FALSE,
    line = list(color = "#10243A", width = 2, dash = "dash"),
    hoverinfo = "skip",
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Adults age 25+ with bachelor's degree or higher (%)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Median household income", tickprefix = "$", separatethousands = TRUE),
    margin = list(l = 75, r = 20, t = 15, b = 65),
    paper_bgcolor = "#FAF7F0",
    plot_bgcolor = "#FAF7F0",
    font = list(family = "DM Sans", color = "#10243A"),
    annotations = list(
      list(
        text = paste0("Pearson r = ", sprintf("%.2f", correlation)),
        x = 0.02,
        y = 0.98,
        xref = "paper",
        yref = "paper",
        xanchor = "left",
        yanchor = "top",
        showarrow = FALSE,
        bgcolor = "white",
        bordercolor = "#C8A66A",
        borderpad = 6
      )
    )
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```
:::

::: {.chart-card}
### Highest degree attainment

Top 10 states by share of adults with a bachelor's degree or higher.

```{r}
#| label: fig-top-education
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

education_bars <- ggplot(
  top_education,
  aes(
    x = bachelors_plus_pct,
    y = reorder(state, bachelors_plus_pct),
    text = paste0(state, ": ", sprintf("%.1f%%", bachelors_plus_pct))
  )
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#C8A66A", width = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Adults age 25+ (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "DM Sans") +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#10243A"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FAF7F0", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FAF7F0", color = NA)
  )

ggplotly(education_bars, tooltip = "text") |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```
:::

## Florida, county by county

::: {.chart-card .map-card}
### Educational attainment in Florida

The map uses the same measure as the state comparison. Sarasota County is highlighted in gold; hover over a county for its education percentage and median household income.

```{r}
#| label: fig-florida-map
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

plot_ly(
  data = florida_counties,
  type = "choropleth",
  geojson = county_geojson,
  featureidkey = "properties.GEOID",
  locations = ~GEOID,
  z = ~bachelors_plus_pct,
  text = ~paste0(
    "<b>", county, "</b>",
    "<br>Adults with bachelor's degree or higher: ",
    sprintf("%.1f%%", bachelors_plus_pct),
    "<br>Median household income: $",
    scales::comma(median_household_income)
  ),
  hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
  colorscale = list(
    c(0, "#10243A"),
    c(0.52, "#82919A"),
    c(1, "#C8A66A")
  ),
  zmin = 20,
  zmax = 50,
  colorbar = list(title = "Bachelor's or higher (%)"),
  marker = list(line = list(color = "white", width = 0.7))
) |>
  add_trace(
    data = sarasota,
    type = "choropleth",
    geojson = county_geojson,
    featureidkey = "properties.GEOID",
    locations = ~GEOID,
    z = ~highlight_value,
    text = ~paste0(
      "<b>Sarasota County</b>",
      "<br>Adults with bachelor's degree or higher: ",
      sprintf("%.1f%%", bachelors_plus_pct),
      "<br>Median household income: $",
      scales::comma(median_household_income)
    ),
    hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
    colorscale = list(c(0, "#C8A66A"), c(1, "#C8A66A")),
    zmin = 0,
    zmax = 1,
    showscale = FALSE,
    marker = list(line = list(color = "white", width = 2))
  ) |>
  layout(
    geo = list(
      scope = "usa",
      fitbounds = "locations",
      projection = list(type = "mercator"),
      bgcolor = "#FAF7F0"
    ),
    margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, t = 10, b = 0),
    paper_bgcolor = "#FAF7F0",
    font = list(family = "DM Sans", color = "#10243A")
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```
:::

## What the pattern suggests

The association across the 50 states is positive (`r sprintf("%.2f", correlation)`), but it is not uniform. **`r above_trend$state`** sits furthest above the fitted line: its household income is higher than the line would predict for its degree share. **`r below_trend$state`** sits furthest below it. These are descriptive outliers, not explanations of why income differs.

The top-10 lists overlap, but not perfectly. High educational attainment tends to accompany higher state median incomes in this comparison; housing costs, industry mix, household structure, migration, and many other factors also differ across states. State averages can hide substantial local variation.

::: {.callout-important}
## Correlation is not causation

This is an ecological, state-level comparison—not evidence that obtaining a degree causes a household's income to rise. It does not adjust for confounding factors or ACS margins of error, and it should not be used to predict individual outcomes.
:::

## Data & methodology

Educational attainment is calculated as the combined estimates for bachelor's, master's, professional, and doctoral degrees in table B15003, divided by the total population age 25 and older. Median household income comes from table B19013. State estimates use one observation per state; the Pearson correlation and ordinary least-squares trend are unweighted.

The 2024 ACS five-year estimates summarize survey responses collected over **2020–2024**; income estimates are in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars. Florida county boundaries come from the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary files.

The 2024 detailed-table files and state reference file are public downloads from the [U.S. Census Bureau ACS Summary File](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/) and [Census state reference file](https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/reference/state.txt). No API key is used.

See the [research notes and reproducibility details](about.qmd) for source links, table variables, and limitations.
